limits: NO REGISTERED CASE FOR THE `unparseable` VERDICT, AND THE CAUSE IS A POLICY COLLISION RATHER THAN AN OVERSIGHT (issue #1110). The gate exits 1 and refuses to render `ok` when a test file cannot be PARSED - #840's examined-nothing rule applied per file instead of per directory, since an unparseable file sits inside `files_scanned` while contributing nothing, so the denominator would otherwise assert an inspection that never happened. That verdict has no case in `cases` above because a fixture for it must be unparseable BY CONSTRUCTION, and pyproject.toml's ruff config excludes only `controls/*/anchors` with the recorded reason "anchors are not linted. Fixtures are." A fixture that cannot lint and a policy that requires fixtures to lint cannot both hold; `make lint` reported 4 syntax errors with the case present. It is the same shape `bad-empty` sidesteps by carrying a README.md rather than a .py. WHAT COVERS IT INSTEAD: tests/test_negative_fixture_preconditions.py drives `checker.main()` - the same entry point this control's invocation runs - in both directions. `test_an_unparseable_file_never_renders_as_a_clean_bill` hides a real unwaived wholesale PATH replacement inside the unparseable file and requires exit 1, the file NAMED, and no `ok -`; `test_the_gate_still_reports_clean_when_every_file_parses` is its positive control, without which a guard that redded everything would satisfy the first perfectly while destroying the instrument. A LANE-LOCAL `.ruff.toml` INSIDE THE FIXTURE DIRECTORY WOULD WORK AND IS DELIBERATELY NOT USED (measured 2026-09-21: 3 errors without it, 1 with it, the unrelated F401 still caught, so the exclusion is real and narrow). It was refused because it takes the exception while leaving the sentence at the policy site true-looking and false: a reader of the root config would believe every fixture is linted, with nothing where the rule lives to say otherwise. A correct guard worked around where the workaround is invisible from the rule is worse than a declared gap. WHAT THE WITHDRAWN CASE ESTABLISHED BEFORE IT WAS REMOVED, recorded here because it was OBSERVED and would otherwise be lost with the deleted directory: the framework tells a CRASHING gate from a DETECTING one (the #946 property) on this gate's own anchor. Pre-fix, `survey_paths` re-parsed unguarded and died with an uncaught SyntaxError, exiting 1 - the same exit code a real detection produces. With the case registered, anchor eae94b5 nonetheless read `missed the known-bad input (blind, as required)`, because the harness keys on `detect_signal` and a traceback emits none. An exit-code-only harness would have scored that crash as a successful detection and the anchor as sighted. WHY THE REFUSAL CARRIES `unknown_signal` AND NOT THE DETECTION MARKER (counter-model review, 2026-09-21, codex/gpt-6-astra). The first version of the unparseable verdict deliberately ENDED its line in this gate's own "nothing was scanned" idiom so `detect_signal` would match it with no regex change - reasoning about the detector's COVERAGE, and missing what the match MEANS. `detect_signal` is how the harness scores a SUCCESSFUL DETECTION, so a parse refusal was counted as the gate catching its planted defect: a case whose NEIGHBOURING file merely failed to parse earned `BAD` even when the planted violation was silently waived, and the control could no longer distinguish detecting our defect from failing to examine a neighbour's. That is detector-contracts question 2 breaking inside the instrument built to answer it, introduced by the fix for a defect of the same class. The refusal now carries #1129's `unknown_signal` marker, checked BEFORE `detect_signal`, and deliberately avoids the words "nothing was scanned" - that phrase would still match `detect_signal`'s second alternative and re-create the collision one layer down, precedence or not. The disjointness is pinned in BOTH directions by tests/test_negative_fixture_preconditions.py::test_a_parse_refusal_is_not_scored_as_a_detection, which reads the patterns out of THIS file rather than hardcoding them, so editing either signal without re-checking the pairing fails there.
